exposure: Maternal age: <30 years (reference group), 30-39 years, 40-44 years, ≥45 years
outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 25,054 euploid singleton pregnancies delivered at a tertiary referral private/mutual health hospital in Barcelona, Spain between January 2007 and June 2017
finding: After adjusting for confounding factors, maternal age ≥ 40 years was independently associated with increased risk of gestational diabetes, c-section, and placenta previa, but not preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Risk of emergency c-section was only increased in women ≥45 years, while the increase in c-section rate in other age groups was due to elective indications.
